brief.headline: SK Hynix overtakes Samsung as Korea's most valuable company; memory supercycle intensifying with DDR5 margins now exceeding HBM
brief.summary: <cite index="38-2,38-3">SK Hynix market cap hit $1.35T on June 22, briefly surpassing Samsung Electronics for first time since 2000, driven by 340% YTD rally versus Samsung's 200%.</cite> <cite index="3-10,3-25">SK Chairman Chey noted HBM margins ~60% while standard DRAM hits ~80%, with Micron CEO confirming non-HBM margins currently exceed HBM as DDR5 profitability surges.</cite> <cite index="15-2,15-7,15-8">TrendForce forecasts conventional DRAM contract prices rising 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026 and NAND 70-75% QoQ, following Q1's record 90-95% DRAM jump and ~60% NAND increase.</cite> <cite index="21-5,21-9">Hyperscalers collectively guiding to ~$700B capex in 2026, nearly double 2025 spend, with Meta, Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon each posting quarterly capex roughly doubling YoY.</cite> <cite index="35-3,35-5">CoWoS supply-demand gap expected to narrow from 20% currently to 10% by end-2026 as TSMC monthly capacity reaches 120-140K wafers, though advanced packaging remains binding constraint through 2027.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: Long SK Hynix / short Samsung. SK Hynix commands 61% HBM market share vs Samsung 17%, captured pricing power in customized AI memory, and holds 70% HBM4 share for Nvidia Rubin (2026). Samsung lags in HBM qualification despite broader diversification. Near-term catalyst asymmetry favors Hynix: Nasdaq ADR listing expected August 2026 broadens investor base, while Samsung faces margin compression in logic/consumer. Risk: valuation delta now material after 340% YTD run; any HBM qual wins at Samsung (Broadcom/Google TPU rumored) or memory price correction post-2026 reverses momentum. Tactical window closes if conventional DRAM margins peak Q2-Q3.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="9-6">BofA forecasts 2026 global DRAM revenue +51% YoY, NAND +45%, with ASPs rising 33% and 26% respectively, defining it as 'supercycle similar to 1990s boom'.</cite> <cite index="17-20,7-15">HBM's 3-to-1 wafer capacity conversion vs DDR5 compresses commodity supply; every HBM ramp directly reduces standard DRAM availability.</cite> <cite index="3-6">Meaningful new DRAM capacity unlikely until 2027 at earliest, with supply constraints underpinning elevated prices through 2026.</cite> <cite index="17-3,17-4">Samsung and SK Hynix (70% of global DRAM) signaled no aggressive capacity expansion, prioritizing profitability over volume.</cite> Diverging margin structure: conventional DRAM now higher-margin than HBM due to scarcity premium, inverting historical economics. Risk: Chinese CXMT expanding DDR5 (5-10% share by decade-end) and hyperscaler demand elasticity if AI ROI questioned.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="6-1,6-2">Samsung and SK Hynix raised HBM3E prices ~20% for 2026 deliveries; supply remains tight as both prioritize HBM4 ramp, with 2026 revenue mix forecast 55% HBM4 / 45% HBM3E starting Q3.</cite> <cite index="9-8">UBS predicts SK Hynix will hold ~70% HBM4 market share for Nvidia Rubin platform in 2026, sustaining leadership into next generation.</cite> <cite index="9-21,9-22">BofA estimates 2026 HBM market $54.6B (+58% YoY); Goldman forecasts HBM demand for ASIC-based AI chips to surge 82%, reaching one-third of market as hyperscalers diversify beyond GPUs.</cite> <cite index="18-11">HBM capacity for 2026 entirely sold out, with manufacturers refusing new orders.</cite> Pricing power intact through 2026; correction risk emerges 2027+ as competition intensifies and capacity expands, per sell-side.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix overtakes Samsung as Korea's most valuable company at $1.35T market cap
news_pulse.implication: Structural shift in Korean semis hierarchy; SK Hynix +340% YTD vs Samsung +200% reflects HBM dominance (61% share) and customized AI memory pricing power. Nasdaq ADR launch Aug 2026 could further re-rate.

news_pulse.headline: Conventional DRAM margins now exceed HBM as DDR5 profitability surges; SK Chairman notes standard chips ~80% vs HBM ~60%
news_pulse.implication: Inverts prior thesis that HBM = highest margin. Scarcity premium in commodity DRAM (HBM cannibalizing wafer capacity) drives record profitability. Validates both Samsung/Hynix pricing discipline; risk if Chinese supply (CXMT DDR5) or hyperscaler pushback emerges.

news_pulse.headline: Q2 2026 DRAM contract prices to rise 58-63% QoQ, NAND 70-75% QoQ, following Q1's record 90-95% DRAM surge
news_pulse.implication: Unprecedented sequential inflation persists; server DRAM +60% QoQ, client SSD +40%. Hyperscaler lock-in via SCAs favors Samsung/Hynix but pressures OEM/consumer segments. Pricing momentum likely peaks Q2-Q3 before 2027 capacity arrives.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscalers guiding ~$700B combined 2026 capex, nearly double 2025; Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon each ~doubled quarterly spend YoY
news_pulse.implication: Structural demand underpinning memory supercycle intact. Two-thirds of capex = short-lived assets (GPUs/CPUs, 3-5yr depreciation), driving HBM/DDR5 demand. Sell-side now penciling >$1T 2027 capex; sustains Samsung/Hynix volume visibility but raises ROI risk if AI monetization lags.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix raise HBM3E prices ~20% for 2026; supply tight as HBM4 ramp prioritized, 55% HBM4 / 45% HBM3E mix forecast
news_pulse.implication: HBM3E pricing power sustained as vendors shift capacity to HBM4 (Nvidia Rubin, AMD MI400). Confirms disciplined supply management; SK Hynix 70% HBM4 share (UBS) vs Samsung catch-up dynamic persists.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap to narrow from 20% to 10% by end-2026; monthly capacity 120-140K wafers vs 35K in late 2024
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS remains binding constraint through 2026 despite 4x capacity ramp; Nvidia holds 60-70% allocation. Easing into 2027 could accelerate HBM attach rates and broaden AI accelerator supply, benefiting both Samsung/Hynix HBM volumes.

news_pulse.headline: Memory prices surged 80-90% QoQ Q4 2025 into Q1 2026 across segments; DDR5 chip spot jumped $6.84 (Sep 2025) to $27.20 (Dec)
news_pulse.implication: Cumulative pricing from late 2025 reached multi-year highs; Samsung/Hynix allocation-only frameworks favor hyperscalers, pressuring smaller OEMs. Spot DDR4 trading above DDR5 in some configs reflects legacy scarcity. Risk: demand destruction in consumer/PC segments.

news_pulse.headline: Micron posted record 81% gross margin in 3QFY26 (up from 75% in 2QFY26), CEO confirms non-HBM margins exceed HBM
news_pulse.implication: Micron's margin trajectory validates Samsung/Hynix profitability thesis. Conventional DRAM scarcity > HBM complexity premium in current cycle. Watch for Samsung/Hynix Q2 2026 earnings (late July) to confirm parallel margin expansion.
